brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Two columns of half-n bases at levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:0,0,0-2 and piece:1,0,0-2), joined by snaps.
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut sit on the cut faces of the level-0 half bases.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2 and bin:1,0,2 are both hex-bin-half-n-full-div2 bins (each split into 2 sections) in the level-2 bases. They have no top covers, so they're open.

finish.summary: I built a three-storey tower, two columns wide. It has two drawers on the bottom storey and two open bins on the top storey. Drawers only fit on the cut face of a half base, and a storey can only stack on the same kind of base. So both columns are north-half bases, three storeys high. I added the second column so there are two drawers, not one. The open sides have solid end caps and the joints are bolted. check_build found no rule errors and the parts don't collide. The build is 27 parts, which the print budget counts as 49 pieces, so it's over the usual guide of about 40. The middle storey is empty space. I didn't add props, because the brief didn't ask for any.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
